title: Edge trajectory onboarding tilepack and microcopy for latency steering
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design a compact onboarding tilepack and supporting screenshots that explain Redwood's region/latency routing logic for the Quickstart flow. Deliverables: 1) hero onboarding tile (static + 3 microanimation states) showing request path routing across multiple edge locations; 2) 4 map microtiles that visualize common routing outcomes (local low-latency, cross-region fallback, cost-preferred routing, cache-hit shortcut); 3) two Console screenshots annotated to show tooltip copy and routing toggle; 4) microcopy strings for onboarding steps and accessible alt text. Constraints: map assets must export as SVG + 2x PNG + WebP, microanimations as Lottie JSON, and final assets must fit the Console static asset budget (max 150KB per tile before compression). Use simplified trajectory lines (bezier arcs) instead of full geodesic rendering to keep export sizes small.
acceptance_criteria: Hero tile exported in SVG, PNG@2x, and WebP, and passes size budget (<=150KB)
Three microanimation states exported as Lottie and include a static PNG fallback
Four map microtiles demonstrate the four routing outcomes and have concise microcopy for Quickstart flows
Two Console screenshots with annotated callouts created and uploaded to Drive and referenced in the PR
Accessibility: all color choices meet AA contrast for text and icons; alt text included for each asset
Engineering sign-off on tile coordinate simplification and runtime performance implications
review_feedback: 2025-03-13 Lina Morales (PM): Tighten hero copy to focus on 'latency-first' decision and reduce jargon; prefer 'automatic region steering' terminology.

2025-03-19 UX Review (M. Gomez): Motion is helpful but can be distracting on initial onboarding — provide a static first frame and optional play control.
